subtype: Approach: relying on one contact for everything [Pitfall]
passage:
Volunteer's note, 4 a.m., school relief centre. Nandini writing.
Avni walked in soaked, with two children, asking for a list of names. Avni's family had scattered in the evening rush: some at the temple hall, some on a bus to a relative. "Uncle Ramesh was going to organise everything," Avni said. But Ramesh's phone had been out of network since dusk and nobody had decided on a place to meet. Hours had gone.
I gave the children dry blankets first, then wrote every name on the board and phoned the ward office and the temple hall. By dawn four more relatives had been found. Avni's voice shook. "We should have named a place."
— Nandini

qa.q: Where was Nandini writing the note?
qa.a: Nandini was writing in the school relief centre at 4 a.m.

qa.q: What was Avni likely feeling when arriving at the relief centre?
qa.a: Avni was anxious and worn out, and worried about the family, which shows in the search for names and in the shaking voice.

qa.q: What could Avni's family arrange before the next emergency?
qa.a: They could agree on a meeting place and a backup contact, and each keep the list on paper.

qa.q: How might Ramesh have felt on learning that the phone had been out of network?
qa.a: Ramesh would probably feel guilty and helpless, since the family had counted on Ramesh to organise everything.

grounding: The note shows a family relying on one relative to coordinate everything, and losing hours when that relative's phone is out of network and no meeting place was set.

passage:
12 August, 11 p.m., Mama's house, Kolhapur
I'm writing this on a borrowed mattress because my hands won't stop shaking. The alert came at five. We all said the same thing: Akash Kaka will tell us what to do. He always does. He has the car, he knows the relief office people. So we waited for his call. At six his phone was out of network. We kept calling. Aaji asked where we were meeting. Nobody knew. Papa thought the temple hall, I thought Akash Kaka's building. We lost three hours going between the two in the rain, with Aaji on the back of the scooter. We finally found each other here at nine, soaked. Tomorrow I'm writing a family meeting point on paper for every single one of us, and a second number to call.
Tanuja

qa.q: How long did the family lose going between the temple hall and Akash Kaka's building?
qa.a: Three hours, in the rain, with Aaji on the back of the scooter.

qa.q: What do Tanuja's shaking hands suggest about how the evening felt?
qa.a: Tanuja was frightened and exhausted, still shaken by hours of not knowing where the family was meeting.

qa.q: What other approach could the family use instead of relying on Akash Kaka?
qa.a: They could agree a written meeting point and a second contact for everyone, so one phone out of network doesn't stop the plan.

qa.q: How might Akash Kaka feel when he learns what happened?
qa.a: He may feel guilty and upset that everyone waited on his phone, even though the network failure wasn't his fault.

grounding: It shows a family assuming one relative will coordinate, so when his phone is out of network nobody knows where to gather and hours are lost.

[Family group, 4.10 p.m.]
Sangeeta: Alert says leave low areas by 6. Where do we go?
Chinmay: Mama will tell us, he's handling it
Sangeeta: Did he say where?
Chinmay: Not yet. He said he'll call everyone
[5.30 p.m.]
Sangeeta: Mama's phone is switched off or not reachable 😰
Chinmay: Same. Maybe the tower is down near his side
Sangeeta: Ma is asking where to go. I have Nani, the kids, two bags
Chinmay: I don't know!! I'm on the bridge, water on the road
[7.45 p.m.]
Sangeeta: We're at the anganwadi hall. Where are YOU?
Chinmay: Stuck at the petrol pump. Road closed. Mama finally messaged, he was at the temple waiting for all of us
Sangeeta: Three hours. We never even agreed a place 😔
Chinmay: Never again. Tomorrow we write down one place and two numbers for everyone.

qa.q: Where was Mama waiting for everyone?
qa.a: Mama was at the temple, waiting for all of them.

qa.q: How was Sangeeta feeling at 5.30 p.m.?
qa.a: Sangeeta was frightened and stressed 😰, responsible for Nani, the kids and two bags with no idea where to go.

qa.q: What would you change first in this family's plan?
qa.a: Agree one meeting place and at least two contact numbers ahead of time, as Chinmay says, so everyone can move even if one phone goes dead.

qa.q: What was the evening like for Mama at the temple?
qa.a: Mama waited at the temple not knowing why nobody came, likely worried and helpless once his phone failed.

grounding: It shows a family relying on one relative to coordinate, losing hours when his phone is unreachable and no meeting place has been agreed.
